roles.title: Machine Learning Engineer
roles.summary: Spearheading development of multiple ML models for diagnostic lung ultrasound, and the labeling and training infrastructure behind them.

highlights.label: faster labeling per video (10 → 2 min) via a PyTorch annotation tracker
training experiments on GCP Vertex AI and the team’s Slurm GPU server
of frames labeled on V7 Darwin infrastructure built from scratch

bullets: Spearheading development of multiple ML models for diagnostic ultrasound that run on-device in real time.
Set up Slurm on the team’s GPU server and ran 500+ training experiments across it and GCP Vertex AI.
Built and led the labeling infrastructure on V7 Darwin (GCP, SQL) from scratch, used to label millions of frames.
Automated clip ingestion into the training database, labeling-sprint setup and pre-label uploads through the V7 Darwin API.
Built a PyTorch tracker propagating Labelbox annotations across frames, cutting labeling time per video 5x (10 to 2 min).

roles.title: Machine Learning Developer (Co-op & Part-time)
roles.summary: Built AI systems and data pipelines to automate the diagnosis of lung ultrasound scans.

highlights.label: sensitivity / specificity of the effusion classifier on a 2-hospital holdout
M-mode images from 140K B-mode videos per dataset version
to build a 1K-clip dataset, down from 1–2 hours

bullets: Led development of an effusion classifier: 0.90 sensitivity, 0.89 specificity on a 239-clip holdout from 2 hospitals (AJEM ’25).
Converted an earlier lung-ultrasound model for on-device inference in Deep Breathe’s mobile apps.
Built Azure/SQL data pipelines (Python, Bash, OpenCV) that ingest, process and version ultrasound data, generating 7.8M M-mode images from 140K B-mode videos per version.
Cut 1K-clip dataset builds from 1–2 hours to minutes: teams now download prebuilt, versioned datasets.
Integrated Weights & Biases into ML projects for training dashboards and evaluation logging.

roles.title: Machine Learning Research Intern
roles.summary: LLM evaluation, RAG and test-data tooling around Kolena’s AI Quality Platform.

highlights.label: RAG answer accuracy on financial PDFs after rebuilt parsing and prompting
less manual review with a fine-tuned LLM judge for Qwen-VL outputs
faster text-dataset creation with a Q&A-drafting tool

bullets: Fine-tuned an LLM judge to rate Qwen-VL descriptions against human preferences, cutting manual review volume 3x.
Raised RAG answer accuracy on financial PDFs from 80% to 93% by rebuilding parsing and prompting (LangChain).
Built a Streamlit + OpenAI SDK tool that drafts Q&A and similar test samples, making text-dataset creation 5x faster.
Shipped CV and NLP metadata extraction (OpenCV, NLTK, spaCy) in Kolena’s AI Quality Platform so users can stratify test sets and find model errors on edge cases; presented it in a webinar.

roles.title: Software Engineering Intern
roles.summary: Shipped activity-recognition models for a fitness app and analyzed user retention.

highlights.label: IMU cheat-detection sensitivity, via feature engineering
workout missions after deploying four motion detectors on AWS EC2
faster CPU inference with lightweight scikit-learn models

bullets: More than doubled IMU cheat-detection sensitivity (25% to 55%) via feature engineering with scikit-learn and SciPy.
Deployed punch, crunch, high-knee and jump detection on AWS EC2, growing the app’s workout missions from 2 to 5.
Sped up CPU inference 1.8x by switching to lightweight scikit-learn models.
Found, via decision-tree analysis of early user data, an onboarding path whose users were 1.5x likelier to be retained.
Built a PHP/MySQL analytics dashboard of user activity growth, used in pitches that secured $1.4M in funding.

roles.title: Researcher
roles.summary: LLM safety under fine-tuning and domain generalization. An undergraduate research assistant until graduating in 2025, now a researcher in the lab.

highlights.label: LoRA and full fine-tuning runs for TamperBench (20K GPU-hours)
open-weight LLMs stress-tested; safeguards fell on all 21

bullets: First-authored TamperBench with FAR.AI (KDD ’26 Oral, top 4.5%): stress-tested 21 open-weight LLMs against 9 tampering attacks in 10K+ LoRA/full fine-tuning runs (20K GPU-hours, up to 8 GPUs); safeguards fell on all 21.
Set TamperBench’s initial roadmap and task split for an 11-author team from 5 institutions.
Quoted in MIT Technology Review and University of Waterloo News (2026) as TamperBench’s lead author.
Created SafeTuneBed (IJCAI ’25 workshop), an open-source toolkit benchmarking LLM safety defenses under fine-tuning.
Built FOND’s training/eval pipelines (T-PAMI ’25); the method lifted tumor-detection accuracy 9% at unseen hospitals.
Co-authored Apple-funded LangDA: state-of-the-art domain-adaptive semantic segmentation with vision-language models (NeurIPS ’24 workshop; Best Vision Paper, CVIS ’24).

more: Co-authored Implicit Stylization for Domain Adaptation (ICLR ’23 Domain Generalization workshop).
